title: Documenta 16 Names Four New Curatorial Team Members
summary: The embattled German exhibition's latest appointments, artist Catherine Opie wins a Yale University award, and Dallas Art Fair partners with … a university?

title: How Édouard Manet's Black Cat Became a Symbol of Modernity
summary: Long associated with witchcraft and bad luck, the black feline became an emblem of artistic rebellion and urban life in 19th-century Paris.

title: This Year's Gay Halloween Celebrates Women's Rights and Wrongs
summary: From the Kelly Clarkson's mechanical bird fiasco to Carrie Bradshaw's Dior newsprint dress, Gay Halloween speaks to the staying power of women's iconic media moments.

title: Why Do Horror Films Have Such a Hold on Our Imaginations?
summary: An exhibition at the Academy Museum explores the transgressive power of scary movies, channeling our deepest fears about life, death, and the unknown.

title: Hell Takes the Form of State Repression in 1971’s “The Devils”
summary: Ken Russell’s film designed by Derek Jarman, newly released in a 4K restoration, mirrors the horrors unfolding outside our windows.

title: Before AI There Was the Octopus
summary: Helsinki-based artist Tuomas Laitinen gives us an intelligence with no central brain, no fixed shape, and no interest in being legible to us.

title: ARTPOWER’s New Platform Helps Artists Build Financial Confidence
summary: Designed to answer one of creative work's toughest questions: "What should I charge?"

title: An Epstein Survivor’s Message for MoMA
summary: Dani Bensky explains why the museum must drop Leon Black from its board. Also: The Vatican is serious about protecting artists from AI.

title: I’m an Epstein Survivor. MoMA Must Drop Leon Black.
summary: Institutions must reckon with the possibility that their prestige can be used to legitimize people whose conduct warrants serious investigations.

title: Vatican Exhibition Series Centers "Fundamentally Human" Art Over AI
summary: A triennale across seven cities expands on Pope Leo XIV's message that artificial intelligence models “lack the affective, relational and spiritual perspective” necessary to create art.

title: Beverly Buchanan at the Raw Edge of Art
summary: Instead of leaving the South behind, the polymath artist carried it into her writings, zines, paintings, and “shack sculptures” that echo the architecture of her childhood.

title: San Francisco’s Galleries Explore Alternative Routes for Survival
summary: Amid a cost-of-living crisis and the closure of local arts organizations, some are turning to different models to foster community, from nonprofit status to retail businesses.

title: Lisa Sanditz’s Seismic Sublime
summary: Her environmental paintings ask: What can we do to change our destiny? What effect can we have on the place we inhabit?

title: Cici Wu's Memory Lanterns
summary: Her flickering, hollow, and bandaged forms trace histories embodied across generations.

title: ​​Tacita Dean’s Truth in Materials
summary: Instead of the slick stream of internet and AI imagery, the moving pictures projected onto a 31-foot-tall column are insistently material.
